verdict.rationale: React's markup is JSX, a JavaScript syntax extension that lives in the same TypeScript file as component logic. Adding @types/react and @types/react-dom gives full React Web TypeScript support, and props can be typed, so markup is type-checked along with the rest of the code rather than in a separate template layer. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that JSX expressions and prop usage are type-checked at compile time, and independent or hands-on corroboration of in-template type errors.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get compile-time type checking inside my component templates, not just script blocks

citations.quote: This markup syntax is called JSX. It is a JavaScript syntax extension popularized by React.
you can get full React Web support by adding @types/react and @types/react-dom to your project.
The key difference when working with a component is that you can provide types for your component's props.
